title: An English Violin by William E. Hill & Sons, London, 1913, labelled William E. Hill & Sons, Makers, 140, New Bond Street, London, 1913, No. 260, the two-piece back of pronounced medium curl descending slightly from the joint, the ribs and head of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour, length of back 14 1/16in. (35.8cm.), and a silver-mounted Violin Bow, in case (3).  Sold with the certificate of W. E. Hill & Son, London, dated 2nd April 1943, stating that the violin is a copy of ‘The Messie’ Stradivari.

An English Violin by Simon Andrew Forster, London, 1856, labelled S. A. (35.9cm.).

(35.7cm.), in case (2).

A Violin, possibly by Lapo di Serafino Casini, labelled Serafino Casini, constante B——, Anno 1930, Firenze, the one-piece back of irregular medium curl, the ribs of medium curl, the head almost plain, the table of medium grain in the centre opening out towards the flanks, the varnish of an orange-brown colour, length of back 14in. (35.5cm.), and a nickel-mounted Viola Bow, in case (3).

A good French Violin, circa 1820, labelled Joannes Baptista Guadagnini Piacentinus fecit Mediolani 175 and Gabriel Lembock reparavit. Viennae Anno 1863, the one-piece back of faint medium curl descending from left to right, the ribs and head of medium to narrow curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a golden-orange colour, length of back 14in. (35.6cm.), in case with outer canvas cover (3).  Sold with the certificate of Hamma & Co., Stuttgart, dated 20th July 1954, stating the violin to be by Giovanni Battista Guadagnini (photographs attached), and with that of Friedrich Böhm, Berlin, dated 27th April 1967, giving the same opinion.

An English Violin by George Craske, Stockport, labelled Made by George Craske (born 1797, died 1888), and sold by W. E. Hill & Sons, London. Special Quality, the two-piece back of almost horizontal narrow curl, the ribs of similar curl, the head plain, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a golden-brown colour, length of back 14 1/16in.
